newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga applies for Angola operatorship.
newsitem.headline: Saga applies for Angola operatorship.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA has applied for operatorship of a deepwater block offshore Angola, the company's weekly newsletter said on Monday.
The area lies in water depths of more than 1,000 metres.

"We can draw on expertise built up off Norway and achieve synergies for coming deepwater exploration drilling in the Norwegian Sea," said Trosteinn Sanness, vice president for international operations.
Saga already has a 14 percent stake in Angolan offshore block 1, which covers 3,993 square km. Hydrocarbons have been found in one of the two wells drilled there so far by operator Shell.
Saga, Norway's largest independent oil company, also holds rights in two small finds, where three-dimensional seismic data have been collected and interpreted.
Saga said further drilling on these discoveries was planned for 1997.
It said operations offshore Angola had expanded considerably over the past couple of years because exploration based on new and existing exploration models had yielded good results.
Political and security conditions also were considerably better, Saga said.
